messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Ref in Eigen 3.2
parts:
OK, I think I understand what's going on with Ref.

The only place it will speed things up is if we are
passing expression templates *with contiguous memory*
to Stan functions which then access the members of those
expression templates exactly once (more on this below).

Suppose there's a function foo(m,...) taking a matrix
argument m. As is, our signature

return_type
foo(Matrix<double,Dynamic,Dynamic>& m, ...);

causes an expression template passed in as m to be
evaluated (in Eigen speak) into a temporary Matrix before
being passed by reference. This requires an allocation
for the temporary Matrix and a data copy, both of which
are relatively expensive.

If we instead define the signature as

return_type
foo(const Ref<Matrix<double,Dynamic,Dynamic> >& m1, ...);

then passing an expression template to foo() will not
require a temporary allocation to pass the argument.

Whether this will help will depend on how many places we
pass expression templates to Stan functions and how
many times they're accessed in the Stan function. I'm thinking
that's not many places. For example, it won't help in the
the generated model code, because we're still going to
have Stan functions return Matrix<...> types, which will
force the allocation/copy.

The one place it would definitely help is in T sum(Matrix<T,...>).

I think it only makes sense to use Ref if we only
access the templates once, at least for agrad::var types.
That's because each use of an agrad::var puts the
operation on the reverse-mode auto-diff stack.
For instance, if we have matrices m1 and m2, and
create the expression template (m1 + m2), then we
really only want to put the element sums, m1[i,j] + m2[i,j], on
the expression stack for auto-dif once. So if the elements of the
expression template are accessed more than once, it's going to be
more efficient to evaluate it into a temporary. This is not
the case necessarily with doubles. Eigen does some template
metaprogramming I don't understand the details of to figure
out when it's best to allocate a temporary. I'm wondering
if we could get better control of this in general using
traits for Eigen that determine operation costs? They're
a lot higher for auto-diff var than for double and fvar is
somewhere in between.

- Bob
